original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Determine the exact paid-call minimum of the two-role endpoint diag([B],[B^-1]), B=X^2Y^2, in the PR #3905 integer-shear alphabet, over all F2 frames, interleaved scalar maps, finite workspace and dirty inputs.
scope_change_reason: This answers the Open next question of PR #3905, a specified nonabelian operation family allowed by this card. It refines the card to one two-role cross-sharing question rather than a new register identity.
bottleneck_link: Side result in the formal register model. It shows that cross-role sharing gives no saving for this inverse pair, so a cheaper inverse-pair word must change the alphabet or gate model. No native conversion, supplier or kappa effect.
stop_rule: Ship the first exact minimum. Do not extend to powers B^k, other alphabets or native implementations.
evidence: verify.py checks the #3905/#5394 gate identity for all 24 legal factors, a complete ordered-subproduct census of all 87,381 words of length at most 8, the exact eight-call identity in M2(F2[G]) with dirty columns, and 11 controls. The lower bound applies the cited #5394 cover theorem to this census.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact paid count of diag([B^k],[B^-k]) for k>=2, and does it always equal 8k?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A cross-role saving for a higher power would be the first sharing gain for an inverse pair in this alphabet.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same ordered-subproduct census at lengths up to 15 for k=2 with pruning by the single-target bound, or prove a general no-sharing lemma from the shortest words for B^k and B^-k.
open_questions.blocked_by: The naive census grows as 4^L; a proof needs a structural argument about subproducts that evaluate to B^k.

open_questions.question: Does the eight-call minimum survive if one adds the order-four element S = X Y^-1 X, or any single extra label, to the paid alphabet?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Identifies which alphabet change, if any, makes inverse-pair sharing profitable.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the census over the five-label alphabet through length seven.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each added label needs its own native implementation and price; the formal count alone is not a supplier.
